questions.question: The average marks obtained by 120 students in an examination is 50. If the average marks of passed students is 70 and average marks of the failed students is 30, then what is the number of students who passed the examination?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Average marks of 120 students = 50.

Average marks of passed students = 70.

Average marks of failed students = 30

**Formula:**

Total marks = number of students * average marks

**Solution:**

⇒ Total marks of 120 students = 120 * 50 = 6000.

⇒ Let the number of students who passed be x.

⇒ Total marks of passed students + total marks of failed students = Total marks of all students.

⇒ 70x + 30(120-x) = 6000.

⇒ 40x = 2400.

⇒ x = 2400 / 40 = 60.

**Therefore, the number of students who passed the examination is 60.**

questions.question: If the average of n quantities is P and the average of m quantities is Q, then the average of (m + n) quantities is:
questions.solution:

The average of n quantities = P 

The average of m quantities = Q

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of all the values/Total no. of values

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

The average of n quantities = P

Sum of the n quantities = nP

The average of m quantities = Q

Sum of m quantities = Qm

Now Average of (m + n) = (nP + Qm)/(m + n)

**∴ The average of (m + n) quantities is (nP+mQ)/(m+n).**

questions.question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 74. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the net deviation method with a base average of 62:

The remaining 18 students have an average of 74, which is a deviation of +12 marks from the base.

Total positive deviation = 18 × 12 = 216 marks.

This extra score is distributed equally among all 30 students = 216 ÷ 30 = +7.2 marks.

Overall average score of the class = 62 + 7.2 = 69.2 marks.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.2 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of students in the class = 30

Average score of 12 students = 62

Number of remaining students = 30 − 12 = 18

Average score of the 18 students = 74

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
 
 12 Students
 Avg: 62
 
 
 
 18 Students
 Avg: 74
 
 
 

 Total = 30 Students
 Class Avg = 69.2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of scores of the first 12 students = 12 × 62 = 744

⇒ Sum of scores of the remaining 18 students = 18 × 74 = 1332

⇒ Total combined score of all 30 students = 744 + 1332 = 2076

⇒ Average score of the class = 2076 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score = 69.2

**∴ The correct answer is 69.2 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two distinct groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have individual averages of A₁ and A₂ respectively, the combined or weighted average is calculated as: (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

To calculate averages quickly, assume a base average and find the total deviation of all other values from it. The final average equals the base average plus the net deviation divided by the total number of items.

questions.question: The average monthly income of the father and mother is Rs. 5,000. The average monthly income of the mother and her son is Rs. 6,000. The average monthly income of the father and his son is Rs. 10,000. Find the monthly income (in Rs.) of the father.

= 10000

= 12000

The monthly income of the father and his son = 2 × 10,000

= 20000

questions.question: The average weight of 10 students is increased by half a kg when one of the students weighing 51 kg is replaced by a new student. Find the weight of the new student.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total increase in weight = Number of students × Increase in average weight

Total weight increase = 10 × 0.5 kg = 5 kg

Weight of new student = Weight of replaced student + Total weight increase

Weight of new student = 51 kg + 5 kg = 56 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 56 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of students = 10

Weight of the student replaced = 51 kg

Increase in average weight = 0.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations

 
 
 Group of 10 Students
 Average increases by 0.5 kg
 
 
 

 51 kg
 Leaves

 
 

 New Student
 Joins

 
 
 Net Weight Increase = 10 × 0.5 kg = +5 kg

**Calculations:**

Let the initial average weight of the 10 students be A kg.

⇒ Total initial weight of the 10 students = 10 × A = 10A

Let the weight of the new student be W kg.

When the 51 kg student is replaced by the new student W, the new total weight becomes:

⇒ New total weight = 10A − 51 + W

The new average weight increases by 0.5 kg, so it becomes A + 0.5 kg.

⇒ New average = (10A − 51 + W) ÷ 10

⇒ A + 0.5 = (10A − 51 + W) ÷ 10

⇒ 10 × (A + 0.5) = 10A − 51 + W

⇒ 10A + 5 = 10A − 51 + W

Subtracting 10A from both sides, we get:

⇒ 5 = W − 51

⇒ W = 51 + 5

⇒ W = 56 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 56 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Replacement Method in Averages

When a person is replaced by a new person, use the formula: New Value = Replaced Value + (Total Number of Items × Change in Average). If the average decreases, the sign before the change becomes negative.

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, their combined average is given by: (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Inclusion & Exclusion Principle

If a new person joins a group and the average increases, their value is strictly greater than the old average. Conversely, if someone leaves the group and the average increases, their value was less than the old average.
</p

questions.question: A class of 25 students took an English test. 15 students had an average score of 80. The other students had an average score of 60. What is the average score of the whole class?

Average score of these 10 students = 60

Average score of the whole class = Total score of all students / Total number of students

**Calculation:**

Total score of 15 students = 15 × 80

⇒ Total score of 15 students = 1200

Total score of 10 students = 10 × 60

⇒ Total score of 10 students = 600

Total score of the whole class = 1200 + 600

⇒ Total score of the whole class = 1800

Total number of students = 25

Average score of the whole class = 1800 / 25

⇒ Average score of the whole class = 72

**The average score of the whole class is 72.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 13 students = 67

Average of first 7 students = 61

Average of last 7 students = 65

**Formula used:**

Average of Nth student = (Sum of first N students + sum of last N students) - sum of all students

**Calculation:**

Sum of 13 students = 67 × 13 = 871

Sum of first 7 students = 61 × 7 = 427

Sum of Last 7 students = 65 × 7 = 455

Average of 7th student = (Sum of first 7 students + sum of last 7 students) - sum of all 13 students

⇒ (427 + 455) - 871

⇒ 882 - 871 = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

Weighted Average

When two groups of sizes N₁ and N₂ have averages A₁ and A₂, the combined average is given by (N₁ × A₁ + N₂ × A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂).

Alligation Rule

A quick method to find the ratio in which two groups are mixed. The ratio of quantity of group 1 to group 2 is (Mean − A₂) : (A₁ − Mean), assuming A₁ > Mean > A₂.

Deviation Method

Reduces calculation by assuming a base average. Net average = Assumed Average + (Total Deviation ÷ Total Items).

⇒ 62/2

questions.question: What will be the average of the odd numbers from 21 to 81?
questions.solution:
Formula used:

The sum of (1 + 2 +.....+ n) = (n(n+1))/(2)

Average = The sum of all number/(Total number)

Calculation:

The sum of odd numbers between 21 to 81,

21 + 23 + 25 + ..........+ 81

⇒ (21 + 0) + (21 + 2) + (21 + 4) +...........+ (21 + 60)

⇒ {21 + 21 + 21 +............(31 times)} + 0 + 2 + 4 + ...........+60

⇒ 31(21) + (0 + 2 + 4 + 6 + ...........+ 60)

⇒ 651 + 2(1 + 2 + 3 +......+ 30)

⇒ 651 + 2[(30(30+1))/(2)]

⇒ 651 + 930

⇒ 1581

Average = The sum of all number/(Total number)

⇒ Average = (1581)/31

⇒ Average = 51

∴ The average of all odd numbers from 21 to 81 is 51.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__****Concept used:**

If the series is in A.P, then

Average of the series = (First term + last term)/2

Calculation:

The consecutive odd numbers are:

21 + 23 + 25 + ..........+ 81

So this series is in A.P

Average of all odd numbers from 21 to 81 = (21 + 81)/2

⇒ 102/2 = 51

∴ The average of all odd numbers from 21 to 81 is 51.

questions.question: The average weight of 8 men is increased by 2 kg when one of them, whose weight is 90 kg, is replaced by another man. What is the weight of the new man?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in total weight = Total members × Increase in average

Net change = 8 × 2 = 16 kg

Since the average increases, the new man is heavier than the replaced man.

Weight of new man = Weight of replaced man + Net change

Weight of new man = 90 + 16 = 106 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 106 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of men = 8

Increase in average weight = 2 kg

Weight of replaced man = 90 kg

 
 Old Man (90 kg)
 
 + 16 kg
 

 8 men × 2 kg
 

 New Man = 106 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original average weight of 8 men be A.

⇒ Total original weight = 8 × A = 8A

⇒ After replacing, the new average becomes (A + 2).

⇒ Total new weight = 8 × (A + 2) = 8A + 16

⇒ Increase in total weight = (8A + 16) − 8A = 16 kg

⇒ This 16 kg increase is strictly due to the weight difference between the new and replaced man.

⇒ Weight of new man = Weight of replaced man + Increase in total weight

⇒ Weight of new man = 90 + 16 = 106 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 106 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Replacement in Averages

When one member is replaced, the weight of the new member can be calculated directly:
New Value = Old Value + (Total Members × Increase in Average)
New Value = Old Value − (Total Members × Decrease in Average)

Addition of a New Member

When a new member joins the group:
New Member = Old Average + (Total Members after addition × Increase in Average)

Removal of a Member

When a member leaves the group:
Removed Member = Old Average − (Remaining Members × Increase in Average)
